main_text.l: tanto plus, quanto à terra longius
exporrigitur, tandemque diminuta prorsus in acumen fastigia-
tur.
Si Calathi aut columnæ figura iaceretur um-
bra, quod fieret si Sol uel minor terra
uel terræ æqualis existeret, ad zodiacum usq; excurreret. Et
si καλαθοειδὴς esset, maximum cœli spacium oc-
cuparet, utpote late explica-
ta: Si κυλινδροειδὴς, tantum tamen in zodiaco spacium
comprehenderet & expleret, quantum terræ
æquaretur. Et ob hanc causam non sola Luna quolibet mense defice-
ret, sed & reliquæ stellæ fixæ &
errantes quæcunq;, soli opponuntur, umbra terræ
quauis nocte hebetarentur & obscurarentur, ac postea
motu primi cœli eductæ rursus illucescerent.
Hæc cum non fieri experientia
perpetua constet, terræ umbra igitur κωνοειδὴς est, & quia
κωνοειδὴν umbram proijcit, ideo multum
cedit Soli magnitudine. Vt enim talis fiat, plus
hemisphærio de globo terreno illuminari, & Solem terra
maiorem esse necesse est, alioqui coni formam um-
bra non acquireret. Illuminari autem 180 partes,
2 s scrupula cum besse, qualium
360 maximus terræ circulus continet propositione
59 libri ultimi Opticæ demonstrat Vitellio. At Lunam terra
superat, quam sola sua umbra & ea quide-
m attenuata
[Last line partly lower right; the text reads "attenuata" with a damaged word.]

page.notes: Scan is a single printed page; the upper and lower sections are the same column. Greek words in the text (καλαθοειδὴς, κυλινδροειδὴς, κωνοειδὴς, κωνοειδὴν) are transcribed as read; the Greek is partly damaged and may need checking. The numeral "1 8 o" was read as 180 and "3 6 o" as 360; "2 s" is 2 scrupula with a degree sign form, and "59" is printed as s9 in the original, read as 59. Show-through and the digitiser URL are omitted.
